2. DESCRIPTION OF THE EXISTING ENVIRONMENT
2.1.1 Land Uses
Page 2-1
Data from Crescent Land and Timber Corporation show that no longleaf pine (P. australis), slash pine (P. elliotti), and loblolly (P. taeda) has been hervested. However, tulip poplar (Liriodendron tulipifera), pitch pine (P. rigida), and Virginia pine (P. virginiana) are frequently harvested and should be added to the list.
Section 2.1.1 has been revised.
2.1.1.1 Recreation
Page 2-3
Highway 107 is located two miles west of the project, not three miles as stated in paragraph three of DEIS.
Section 2.1.1.1 has been revised.
Page 2-4
Paragraph four, the public access areas being developed initially around the reservoir should be four, not five as stated in the DES. See Exhibit R, sheet 1.
Section 2.1.1.1 has been revised.
2.1.2 Topography, Physiography, and Geology
Page 2-5
The last sentence in paragraph tro should be reworded to read: "They are folded, faulted, crushed, and sheared, all of which has accelerated their weathering and decomposition to maximum depths in excess of 100 feet in certain areas", per Exhibit V, Appendix 1, Table 1.
See revised Section 2.1.2.
Paragraph four states that natural materials available for construction appear marginal and will require careful design and proper construction control. Investigations have shown that adequate materials are available, per the License Application, Section 5, Pages 6 and 7 and Exhibit V, Appendix 1, Table 3.
Staff feels this sentence is accurate as stated and requires no revision.
Paragraph five mentions concern regarding seepage losses through the foundation rock. A grout curtain will be placed in the creek bottom and blanketing with soil will be used where soil cover over weathered rock is relatively thin. See Exhibit W, Appendix i.
Section 2.1.2 has been revised.
2.1.3 Solls
Page 2-6
The first sentence in paragraph four should be reworded to read: "These soils are subject to rapid erosion when exposed".
Section 2.1.3 has been revised.
